title: Using Vision + Language Models to Predict Item Difficulty

live_model.evidence: "We used the GPT-4.1-nano model via the OpenAI API, leveraging its multimodal capabilities." (three modeling approaches: text-only, vision-only, multimodal)

prompt.location: Sec 2.2 (Modeling Approach): system-prompt content described per approach (feature list for text-only, vision-only, and multimodal conditions); Pydantic-structured JSON output
prompt.note: The features each system prompt instructs the model to consider are listed; the literal system-prompt string is paraphrased, not quoted.

claim.metric: mean absolute error (MAE) between predicted and actual item easiness, multimodal (vision+text) model
claim.location: Abstract/Sec 2.1: "the multimodal approach...yields the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) (0.224), outperforming the unimodal vision-only (0.282) and text-only (0.338) approaches"; N=154 validation subset

data.source: Data-visualization-literacy item-response dataset (Verma and Fan 2025), items from WAN/GGR/BRBF/VLAT/CALVI assessments

notes: Small, cheap, well-specified single-author study; GPT-4.1-nano is called directly via the OpenAI API with structured (Pydantic/JSON) output for 3 feature-set conditions over a 154-item validation subset, plus a held-out test set (MSE 0.10805) for the best multimodal model.
